subject.title: Feature: Telegram Reactions - Two-Way Support with Prompt Guidance

question: Should Telegram reaction prompt control remain unified under existing `reactionLevel`, or should OpenClaw add the requested separate `reactionGuidance: off|minimal|full` config with documented precedence and defaults?
rationale: The request adds a public prompt-affecting config surface that overlaps current `reactionLevel` behavior and related reaction default/wake/persistence issues, so automation should not choose the product contract.

options.title: Unify Under reactionLevel
options.body: Keep one prompt-control source, add incoming soft-CTA guidance and notification gating through the existing reaction-level policy, and avoid a parallel config unless decoupling is proven necessary.

options.title: Add reactionGuidance
options.body: Implement the requested separate option with explicit composition rules for `reactionLevel` and `reactionNotifications`, generated metadata, docs, and upgrade tests.

options.title: Defer Prompt Expansion
options.body: Keep current outgoing-only prompt guidance and leave incoming reaction interpretation to broader reaction feedback or wake-design work.

recommendation.title: Unify Under reactionLevel
recommendation.body: Keep one prompt-control source, add incoming soft-CTA guidance and notification gating through the existing reaction-level policy, and avoid a parallel config unless decoupling is proven necessary.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest recent history across prompt policy, Telegram plugin routing, and prior triage on the exact config/prompt gap.
